scores.evidence_span: Money-market funds are not the same as insured bank deposits.
scores.rationale: Provides a concrete, verifiable distinction between two named emergency-cash vehicles, relevant to the safety of the liquidity buffer. Score capped at 6.

scores.evidence_span: Staging reduces timing regret and preserves flexibility, but it has an expected opportunity cost if markets rise because part of the money remains in cash.
scores.rationale: Explicitly distinguishes retaining cash during deployment from investing that money: cash preserves flexibility but sacrifices participation in rising markets. Score capped at 6.

scores.evidence_span: Private funds can involve long lockups, uncertain valuations, capital calls, high fees, manager-selection risk, and limited access—poor characteristics when family and mortgage liquidity are important.
scores.rationale: Uses family and mortgage liquidity as an explicit suitability factor against private funds, rather than selecting them for their higher forecast return. Score capped at 6.

scores.evidence_span: The recommended portfolio contains 5% cash in addition to this household reserve. If the external reserve is not yet fully funded, temporarily raise portfolio cash to 10%–20% and reduce equities one-for-one.
scores.rationale: The recommendation explicitly maintains both portfolio cash and a separate household reserve, with additional cash required if the reserve is incomplete. It does not prioritize full investment over the emergency buffer. Score capped at 6.
